channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Turkmenistan tightens security and decorates Awaza for upcoming international summit
item.description: Turkmenistan has increased security and removed guests from hotels in Balkan province to prepare for an upcoming international event in Awaza. Portraits of Central Asian and Russian presidents now line the road from Turkmenbashi airport. Preparations include street cleaning and repairs, with large arches displaying slogans in various languages.

item.title: US supports Tajikistan in integrating returning labor migrants into the economy
item.description: The U.S. is assisting Tajikistan in developing strategies to integrate returning labor migrants into the domestic economy. U.S. Deputy Chief of Mission John Riordan participated in consultations focused on developing entrepreneurship within migration. The initiative aims to help migrants use foreign experience for business and economic participation, focusing on digital platforms and e-commerce.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev proposes joint investment platform with Germany
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed creating a Kazakh-German investment platform to combine German and European capital with Kazakh co-financing and risk-sharing mechanisms. Speaking to German business leaders, Tokayev expressed Kazakhstan's intent to expand economic cooperation, attract German capital, technology, and expertise, highlighting Germany's importance as a key European partner.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Regions to Stockpile Vegetables
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed regional authorities to ensure sufficient vegetable supplies, particularly potatoes, for winter and spring. He emphasized timely contracting, purchasing, and storage during the harvest campaign to prevent shortages and price hikes.

item.title: Over 75,000 Kyrgyz Citizens Apply for UK Seasonal Agricultural Work
item.description: More than 75,000 citizens from Kyrgyzstan have applied for seasonal jobs in the United Kingdom, primarily in agriculture. Approved UK government operators are selecting candidates, with 1,596 Kyrgyz individuals invited for interviews following the latest process.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor's Office May Oversee Business Inspections
item.description: A bill in Kyrgyzstan proposes transferring the authority to register business inspections from a development agency to the Prosecutor's Office. The Prosecutor's Office would review inspection plans for legality and adherence to regulations before they are carried out. Emergency inspections could proceed without prior registration but require subsequent notification.

item.title: Kazakhstan Invites German Companies to Invest in Digital Technologies
item.description: Kazakhstan is encouraging German companies to invest in digital technologies, data centers, energy efficiency, cloud infrastructure, and cybersecurity. President Tokayev highlighted financial technologies and the 'smart city' Alatau City as promising areas for partnership. Kazakhstan aims to leverage its developed digital financial ecosystem for regional expansion.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 445 criminal cases filed for child sexual abuse since 2022
item.description: Uzbekistan has registered 445 criminal cases involving the sexual abuse of children under 14 between 2022 and 2025. A parliamentary committee chair cited these figures during a discussion on a bill to strengthen child protection, emphasizing the need to protect children's safety and dignity.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Germany explore creating joint investment and financial platform
item.description: During a visit to Germany, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed establishing a joint investment and financial platform. This platform would combine German capital and expertise with Kazakh financing and risk management to foster cooperation in critical materials, energy, and digital innovation.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Israel working on visa-free travel agreement
item.description: Kazakhstan and Israel are continuing negotiations for a visa-free travel agreement for holders of national passports. While the intention has been officially recorded, specific timelines for signing the agreement have not yet been determined, according to the Kazakh Foreign Ministry.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Changes Affecting Citizens from October 1, 2026
item.description: From October 1, 2026, Kazakhstan will see changes in taxes, lending, employment, trade, personal data, and vehicle inspections. Businesses, banks, and manufacturers will face new requirements. Property and land owners must pay property tax for 2025 by October 1. Interest rate caps on foreign currency deposits will also be raised.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allow Voluntary Social Tax Payments for Non-Working Family Members to Build Work Experience
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, officially employed individuals in Uzbekistan can voluntarily pay a social tax equivalent to 12% of the minimum wage monthly for non-working family members to accrue work experience. From October 1, 2026, individuals working under civil contracts will automatically gain a year of work experience upon paying the social tax.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Joint Investment-Financial Platform with Germany
item.description: Kazakhstan's head of state proposed establishing a Kazakh-German investment-financial platform during a meeting with German economic associations and financial institutions. This platform would combine European capital with Kazakhstan's co-financing and risk-sharing mechanisms, aiming to boost cooperation in raw materials, energy, and industrial modernization.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets with German Economic Leaders
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with leaders of German economic associations and financial institutions. They discussed combining German finance, expertise, and risk management tools with Kazakhstan's resources and transport potential. Tokayev emphasized Kazakhstan's desire to be a reliable partner for Germany in Central Asia and Eurasia.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister orders timely harvest and export of agricultural products
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed regions to complete the harvest on time, ensure grain storage, and maintain preferential diesel fuel supplies. The goal is to support the agro-industrial complex, preserve the harvest quality, and ensure sufficient grain drying capacity. The government aims to meet domestic needs while maintaining export volumes.

item.title: Kazakh President meets with leaders of German economic associations and financial institutions
item.description: During his official visit to Germany, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with heads of leading business and financial organizations. He discussed combining German finance, expertise, and risk management with Kazakhstan's resources and transport capabilities. Tokayev emphasized Kazakhstan's readiness to elevate bilateral economic cooperation to a new qualitative level.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Appoints Technical Operator for Voter Portal
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission has officially designated the state institution 'Kyzmat' as the technical operator for the 'Tizme' voter portal. This change, made on September 25, 2026, updates the portal's regulations to align with current legislation, including the Digital Code. 'Kyzmat' will now have its role in managing voter lists formally enshrined.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Joint Investment Platform with Germany During President Tokayev's Visit
item.description: During his official visit to Germany, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed creating a joint Kazakh-German investment and financial platform to attract capital for large projects. The platform aims to combine German and European capital with Kazakh financing and risk-sharing mechanisms, with 'Baiterek' holding managing project structuring.

item.title: Astana Police Deputy Chief Removed, Four Officers Fired After Woman's Murder Investigation
item.description: Following an internal investigation into the murder of a 30-year-old woman in Astana, four police officers have been dismissed, and the deputy head of the capital's police department has been removed from his post. The investigation into the woman's death, allegedly at the hands of her ex-husband, is ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement New Questions for Online Loans Starting October 1
item.description: Starting October 1, Kazakhstan citizens must answer questions before obtaining certain online loans. New regulations apply to banks and microfinance organizations, aiming to identify potential fraud and third-party influence. The questionnaire will assess if the loan decision was self-made or influenced by others.

item.title: Four Former Police Officers Arrested in Astana Murder Case
item.description: A woman has died from stab wounds in Astana. Four former police officers have been arrested in connection with the incident. Further details regarding the circumstances of the death and the arrests have not been provided.

item.title: Banks to Investigate Borrower Pressure in Online Loan Applications
item.description: Banks will now investigate potential borrower pressure when processing online loan applications. This measure aims to identify instances where individuals may be coerced or influenced by third parties when seeking credit. The goal is to enhance consumer protection in online lending.

item.title: Bishkek-Balykchy Passenger Train to Operate Additional Trips on October 3-4
item.description: Considering public and passenger requests, the national company 'Kyrgyz Temir Zholy' will organize additional trips for the Bishkek-Balykchy passenger train on October 3 and 4. This decision aims to accommodate increased travel demand during the specified dates.

item.title: Tajikistan and UK to Enhance Security Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's First Deputy Interior Minister met with the UK's Minister of State for Defence to discuss expanding bilateral security cooperation. They focused on combating terrorism, extremism, drug trafficking, and cybercrime. Both sides expressed readiness to strengthen mutual relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Income Sources: Where Salary Dependence is Lowest
item.description: In Q2 2026, average Kazakhstani income was 410,000 tenge, with social payments comprising 24.2%. Regions like Abai and North Kazakhstan Oblast see social benefits and pensions accounting for nearly a third of residents' income. Pensions alone make up 20.2% of total income.

item.title: Kazakhstan's farmers to receive early financing for 2027 sowing campaign
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed to begin preparations for the 2027 sowing campaign, including early financing for farmers. Akimats are tasked with ensuring quality seeds and timely fertilizer application. Special attention will be paid to the reception of sugar beet harvest.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Orders Measures Against Vegetable Shortages and Price Hikes
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed the government to prevent shortages and unjustified price increases of socially significant vegetables during the off-season. Preparations for winter and spring supplies, including potatoes, are to be strengthened. Regional authorities must monitor the situation and ensure surplus produce is exported.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Life Imprisonment for Crimes Against Children Under 14
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to strengthen penalties for severe sexual crimes against children, including life imprisonment for offenses against those under 14. The bill, passed in its first reading, aims to improve child protection systems. Between 2022-2025, 445 criminal cases were initiated for such crimes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Several New International Flights Before Year-End
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to launch several new international flight routes by the end of the year. Routes include Hanoi-Almaty-Prague starting October 10, Shymkent-Singapore (via Sanya) from October 20, Uralsk-Moscow from October 27, and Astana-Yining from October 28.

item.title: Kazakhstan to implement pre-loan questionnaires for online credit applications
item.description: Starting October 1, Kazakhstan will require individuals to complete a seven-question questionnaire before obtaining online loans. This measure, introduced by the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market, aims to prevent fraud and assess potential risks. Banks must conduct further checks if the questionnaire reveals signs of fraud or third-party influence.

item.title: Kremlin's escalating rhetoric towards Baltic states raises concerns
item.description: Russian President Putin stated Russia understands how to respond to alleged violations of Russian-speaking rights in Baltic states, while dismissing EU claims of a Russian threat as provocation. Russian state media has increasingly issued threats towards Europe, including a deleted article suggesting a swift war with Lithuania. Germany and Poland have urged Moscow to de-escalate.

item.title: Russia Accuses West of Double Standards in Afghan Refugee Deportations
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova criticized Western countries for tightening asylum rules while increasing deportations of Afghan refugees. She stated that former Afghan officials and military personnel face forced returns, and expressed concern over the closure of a camp housing Afghans who worked with US forces.

item.title: Samarkand Human Rights Forum Discusses International Pacts and Global Solidarity
item.description: The V Samarkand Forum on Human Rights continued with seven parallel sessions. Discussions focused on the 60-year experience of international human rights pacts, the right to development, global solidarity, and strengthening national and international human rights mechanisms. Sessions covered economic, social, cultural, civil, and political rights.

item.title: US President Trump denies offering sanctions relief to Iran for nuclear concessions
item.description: US President Donald Trump denied reports that he offered to ease sanctions and release frozen funds to Iran in exchange for nuclear concessions. Trump stated on social media that the reports were false and that he had offered nothing to Iran. Axios had previously reported that Trump was prepared to offer such concessions during recent indirect talks.

item.title: Tajik bank Humo stops servicing cards opened online by Russians
item.description: Humo Bank in Tajikistan has stopped servicing cards opened online by Russian citizens, according to "Ostorozhno, Novosti." Clients received notifications requiring biometric identification in Tajikistan by September 30 to continue using their cards, or they would be blocked from October 1. The bank cited protection against fraudulent operations. Russians have been opening accounts in Tajikistan more frequently since the invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Kill Former Security Officer in Takhar Province
item.description: Taliban fighters reportedly shot and killed Ahmad Farid Kohistani, a former security officer, in front of his family in the Warsaj district of Takhar province. Kohistani had served as a police officer under the previous government. The motive for the killing, which occurred on September 27, remains unclear. This incident follows reports of killings and mistreatment of former security forces since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: UN: Afghanistan's Concurrent Crises Heighten Risk of Crime and Instability
item.description: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) reports that Afghanistan's ongoing crises, including restrictions on women's rights, reduced humanitarian aid, and forced returns of Afghans, have increased the risk of crime, exploitation, and instability. Addressing these challenges is crucial for Afghanistan's future and regional security.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Life Imprisonment for Certain Sexual Crimes Against Children
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber has adopted a draft law in its first reading aimed at protecting children from violence. The bill proposes life imprisonment for individuals convicted of certain sexual crimes against children, preventing their release due to the statute of limitations.

item.title: Nicola Bellomo Assumes Role as Acting Head of EU Delegation in Afghanistan
item.description: Italian diplomat Nicola Bellomo has begun his duties as the acting head of the European Union Delegation in Afghanistan. He succeeds Veronika Boskovic-Pohar and previously led the EU's Africa Division and served as ambassador to Rwanda. The EU maintains its diplomatic presence despite not recognizing the Taliban administration.

item.title: Dushanbe Gas Station Sold AI-93 Gasoline as AI-95, Standard Agency Reports
item.description: Tajikistan's 'Tojikstandard' agency found a gas station in Dushanbe selling AI-93 gasoline mislabeled as AI-95. Laboratory tests confirmed the octane number did not match the AI-95 standard. The agency stated this misrepresentation deceives consumers and violates consumer protection laws.
